title: Switching of transcriptional control from interferon regulatory factor 2 to interferon regulatory factor 1 drives innate immune cell activation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found GEO SuperSeries GSE260808 (173 samples, public 2026-08-25; subseries GSE260804 RNA-seq 24 samples, GSE260807/GSE268648 ChIP-seq, GSE318053 scRNA-seq 2 samples) by GEO title search. Filelist: 120 per-sample gene count tables, 46 peak files, 2 MTX, RAW.tar 423 MB. Opened GSM8124759 counts (52,636 Ensembl mouse genes; columns name/count/width/rpkm) and GSM8124830 IRF2 WT ChIP peaks (6,878 MACS2 narrowPeak rows, mm10).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Paper is paywalled with no PMC full text; experimental design (knockouts, TLR stimulation, SPOP mechanism) comes from the abstract only. The GEO-to-paper link is inferred from matching titles, as no accession was text-mined.

a1_downloadable.note: Public on GEO with no login; I downloaded one count file and one peak file.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: This is a mechanistic knockout/ChIP study with no outcome column. Any label (e.g. a genomic region is IRF1- vs IRF2-bound, or a gene is an IRF1-dependent ISG, meaning interferon-stimulated gene) would have to be built by calling peaks, defining negatives and computing differential expression across files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Peak coordinates (mm10 genome build) and Ensembl gene IDs are present; sequence features would come from the reference genome.

a4_units_stated.note: Raw counts and RPKM (reads per kilobase per million) columns are named in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: 173 GEO samples spread over many conditions, with roughly 2–4 replicates per condition. Peak-level rows (6,878 IRF2 peaks in one replicate) exist, but only as a label built from peaks.

a6_fits_laptop.note: The processed tables total about 423 MB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Can't be checked without the full text; GEO counts are internally consistent.

a8_label_provenance.note: Measurements are direct (RNA-seq, ChIP-seq), but labels would be derived by peak calling and differential-expression thresholds.

backbone.name: Not applicable (rejected); a DNA language model such as Nucleotide Transformer would be the obvious choice for peak sequences

honest_claim_h3: At best: a model trained on one lab's mouse macrophage ChIP-seq separates IRF1-favoured from IRF2-favoured binding sites in that cell type, a task that general sequence-to-binding models already cover.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around immune-gene control regions to predict whether IRF1 or IRF2 occupies them in mouse immune cells.
plain_idea.train_on: DNA sequence windows under transcription-factor binding peaks; one IRF2 replicate has 6,878 peaks, while non-bound negatives and IRF1-vs-IRF2 contrasts would have to be built.
plain_idea.predict: Binding by IRF1 versus IRF2 (or knockout-driven gene induction), measured by ChIP-seq (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing) and RNA-seq in mouse macrophages.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: This could show whether the IRF2-to-IRF1 switch has a sequence signature. But the labels must be constructed from a few replicates in one lab, and predicting binding from sequence is a crowded task.

ml_idea: Rejected. The only plausible task is building IRF1/IRF2 binding labels from peak files for a sequence model, which is one lab and one cell type with labels that must be constructed.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from GEO file sizes only; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count replicates per condition in the GSE260808 sample table; already seen to be about 2–4.

verdict_reason: Mechanistic mouse knockout study: the GEO data (173 samples over many conditions, about 2–4 replicates each) has no label column. Any target would be built from peak calls or differential expression (fails A2, A5).
